Usage: amp config model-providers [options] [command]

Manage model provider keys and subscriptions (bring your own key or subscription). Connections are tried in priority order (lowest number first); the first active connection whose model mapping includes a model serves it.

Commands:

  list                      List model provider keys and subscriptions in priority order
  activate                  Activate a model provider key (only subscriptions replace the active connection of the same
                            type)
  deactivate                Deactivate a model provider key
  set-priority              Change where a connection sits in the model routing precedence order
  show                      Show complete non-secret model provider connection data as JSON
  delete                    Delete a model provider key or subscription
  test                      Test a model provider key or subscription
  check-access              Check which model provider serves a model by running a small inference
  add-router                Add an AI model router and select the models routed through it
  edit-router               Edit an AI model router
  setup-guide               Explain how to obtain the credential an AI model router needs
  edit-key                  Edit a model provider API key name or model mapping
  add-chatgpt-subscription  Link your ChatGPT subscription to Amp as a model provider by signing in to OpenAI in your
                            browser

Options:

  --json
      print the complete non-secret connection data as JSON
  --workspace
      list keys of your current workspace instead of your user


Docs: https://ampcode.com/docs/customize/model-routing

Usage: amp config model-providers add-router [options] <router>

Add an AI model router and select the models routed through it

Arguments:

  <router>
      Provider to add: ollama-cloud, openrouter, vercel, cloudflare, google-cloud-agent-platform, google-ai-studio,
      amazon-bedrock, opencode-go, or custom-url

Options:

  --name <name>
      custom connection name
  --model-mapping <mapping>
      newline- or comma-separated provider/model patterns served by this connection, such as */* or openai/gpt-5.6-*;
      prefix a pattern with - to exclude it, and add "-> provider-model-id" after an exact model ID to override the
      model ID sent to the provider (the default when not given is all supported models)
  --api-key-file <path>
      read the API key from a file, or '-' for stdin
  --active
      activate the model router after creating it
  --no-active
      create the model router without activating it
  --personal
      add the model router to your personal account
  --workspace
      add the model router to your current workspace
  --api-format <format>
      custom-url API format: chat-completions, responses, anthropic-messages, google-genai
  --base-url <url>
      custom-url base URL, using HTTPS
  --cloudflare-account-id <id>
      Cloudflare account ID
  --cloudflare-gateway-id <id>
      Cloudflare AI Gateway ID
  --workload-identity-provider <resource-name>
      google-cloud-agent-platform workload identity pool provider that trusts Amp, as
      projects/PROJECT_NUMBER/locations/global/workloadIdentityPools/POOL/providers/PROVIDER
  --google-cloud-project <id>
      google-cloud-agent-platform Google Cloud project ID to bill (default: the pool's project)
  --google-cloud-location <location>
      google-cloud-agent-platform location, a region ID or global
  --iam-role-arn <arn>
      amazon-bedrock IAM role that trusts Amp, as arn:aws:iam::ACCOUNT_ID:role/NAME
  --aws-region <region>
      amazon-bedrock AWS region of the Bedrock endpoint
  --headers <json>
      custom request headers as JSON [name, value] pairs
  --query-params <json>
      custom-url query parameters as a JSON object
  --router-options <json>
      typed request options for the selected dedicated gateway


Examples:
  printf %s "$OPENROUTER_API_KEY" | amp config model-providers add-router openrouter --workspace --api-key-file - --model-mapping anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.6 --router-options '{"provider":{"zdr":true}}'
  amp config model-providers add-router google-cloud-agent-platform --workspace --workload-identity-provider projects/123456789012/locations/global/workloadIdentityPools/amp-inference/providers/amp-inference --model-mapping anthropic/claude-opus-4-6

google-cloud-agent-platform (Google Cloud Agent Platform, formerly Vertex) authenticates with Workload Identity Federation instead of a key: pass --workload-identity-provider, not --api-key-file. Run `amp config model-providers setup-guide google-cloud-agent-platform --workspace` for the issuer and subject to register and the gcloud commands. It serves no models until you pass --model-mapping with the models that should use it.

  amp config model-providers add-router amazon-bedrock --workspace --iam-role-arn arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/AmpBedrock --aws-region us-east-1 --model-mapping anthropic/claude-opus-4-6

amazon-bedrock authenticates by assuming an IAM role with OIDC federation instead of a key: pass --iam-role-arn, not --api-key-file. Run `amp config model-providers setup-guide amazon-bedrock --workspace` for the issuer and subject to register and the aws commands. It serves no models until you pass --model-mapping with the models that should use it.

Model mapping syntax and custom-url request paths: https://ampcode.com/docs/customize/model-routing#model-mappings
